# Learning from complex health data

[My work connects statistical methodology with questions in environmental and population health: how exposures act together, where we observe outcomes, and whose health is represented in our data.]{.lede}

::: {.area-content}
## Causal dimension reduction

Environmental exposures occur in mixtures. I develop methods for summarizing multiple continuous exposures while retaining the information needed to study their joint causal effects.

With Howard H. Chang and Razieh Nabi, I developed causal sufficient dimension reduction, a framework that represents a causal exposure–response surface through a smaller set of exposure summaries. Our preprint applies this approach to maternal PFAS exposure and infant birth weight. The accompanying **csdr** R package makes the methodology available for use in other studies.

::: {.related}
[Causal sufficient dimension reduction (2026 preprint)](publications.qmd#hsiao-2026-csdr) · [csdr package](https://github.com/tXiao95/csdr)
:::

## Spatial statistics & preferential sampling

Where data are collected can be informative about the process being studied. My spatial research addresses preferential sampling and the design of disease surveillance systems.

With Lance Waller, I developed inverse sampling intensity weighting for preferential sampling adjustment, implemented in the **ISIW** R package. Related work considers the balance between access, precision, and equity when allocating testing sites, with an application to COVID-19 surveillance in Atlanta.

::: {.related}
[Inverse sampling intensity weighting (2026)](publications.qmd#hsiao-2026-isiw) · [Adaptive test site allocation (2025)](publications.qmd#hsiao-2025-allocation) · [ISIW package](https://github.com/tXiao95/ISIW)
:::

## Environmental epidemiology

I collaborate on studies of environmental exposures and reproductive and respiratory health. This work includes time-to-event analysis of ambient air pollution and spontaneous abortion, and a study of maternal air pollution exposure and stillbirth in Georgia.

My work on temperature and respiratory emergency department visits uses causal mediation analysis to investigate the role of ambient ozone. These applications motivate methods that can account for complex exposure patterns and clarify pathways linking the environment to health.

::: {.related}
[Air pollution & spontaneous abortion (2026)](publications.qmd#hsiao-2026-aje) · [Air pollution & stillbirth (2026)](publications.qmd#li-2026-stillbirth) · [Temperature & ozone mediation (2026 preprint)](publications.qmd#li-2026-ozone)
:::

## Informative missingness & health data

Electronic health records and self-service health kiosks offer opportunities to study population health, while raising questions about who is observed and how different sources can be combined. My current interests include informative missingness and data fusion in these settings.

Collaborative work has examined blood pressure measurements from retail health kiosks, county-level hypertension prevalence, awareness, and control, and estimates of overweight and obesity using electronic health records and kiosks. These studies motivate my interest in the observation processes underlying routinely collected health data.

::: {.related}
[Retail kiosk blood pressure (2025)](publications.qmd#hsiao-2025-jama) · [County hypertension estimates (2026)](publications.qmd#hsiao-2026-hypertension) · [Obesity estimates from EHR & kiosks (2026)](publications.qmd#varghese-2026-obesity)
:::

## Research software

Alongside **[csdr](https://github.com/tXiao95/csdr)** and **[ISIW](https://github.com/tXiao95/ISIW)**, I maintain **[gallery](https://cran.r-project.org/package=gallery)**, an R package for generating test matrices for numerical experiments.
